Problem: The three triangles in the figure intersect at 12 different points. What is the maximum number of intersection points of any three triangles?

<reflection>
The problem asks for the maximum number of intersection points of three triangles. To maximize the total number of intersection points, one must consider how the triangles intersect each other.
A pair of triangle boundaries can intersect in up to 6 points, since each of the 3 sides of one triangle can intersect each of the 3 sides of the other at most once.
Use the correct pairwise maximum of 6 intersection points and multiply by the 3 pairs of triangles, assuming no three sides meet at the same point.
</reflection>
